_comment_sells_as: PRICED ABOVE THE CATEGORY'S CREDIBILITY FLOOR, DELIBERATELY. This read $800-2,000/mo. The market research is blunt about that band: a GEO retainer under ~$3k/mo reads as classic SEO wearing a new label, because real multi-engine weekly tracking costs the agency actual infrastructure. Boutique GEO specialists sell at $3-8k with a three-month minimum. Pricing under the floor does not win the deal, it disqualifies the pitch — the buyer's read is that nobody is really probing anything. This is what the founder RESELLS at, not what Mycel charges them.
_comment_schedules: MONDAY, NOT 'EVERY 604800 SECONDS'. This was `{kind:'every', seconds:604800}`, which counts a week from the last RUN rather than from a weekday — so one retry, one redeploy, or the scheduler's catch-up fire on boot walks the client's report off Monday and onto Tuesday, then Wednesday, permanently, with the schedule reporting healthy the whole way. 'The Monday report' is a promise about a day of the week. 07:00 UTC so it is waiting when European clients open their laptop, and it is the founder's Monday morning too — the one day the week's number should already be on the desk.
